grade_rationale.text: The only verified people is the Russians: Ralston calls Kikimora the Russian word for the incubus, and Afanasyev calls kikimora a Russian word.
Máchal independently records the Kikimoras in Russia as tiny female household beings behind the oven, fond of spinning, with no reference to Afanasyev on that passage.
Afanasyev, across two volumes counted as one source, records the kikimoras behind the stove, spinning, invisible, and the incantation and Kostroma hen-house stones against them.

Ralston depends on Afanasyev for the derivation of the name ("says Afanasief"), but his account of the kikimori as souls of unchristened or cursed girls cites no one on that passage, so it counts as a third independent source.
One people with several independent sources (Máchal, Ralston, Afanasyev) is regional.
